clue.text: Star actor I cast as one of the best?

indicators.note: to cast metal is to pour it into a new shape, so these letters are recast in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A theatre director wonders whether to cast a leading actor as one of an elite group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' is the anagram signal applied to STARACTORI. The definition rests on the Greek root aristos, 'best', with the question mark owning the loose sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from Greek aristos, meaning best, so a member of the nobility is literally one of the finest.

clue.text: Impenetrable song by drunk

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
tight is informal for drunk

explanation.surface: A tipsy singer's performance is beyond understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sealed so that nothing can get through is impermeable, hence impenetrable.

clue.text: Confiscate one's money, initially — sterling

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I, and 'one's' reads as 'one has'

indicators.note: initially says take only the opening letter of the word money

parts.note: the pound is the unit of sterling currency

explanation.surface: An official seizes someone's cash, starting with British pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To impound is to seize and hold property by legal authority, a synonym for confiscating it.

clue.text: It doesn't look good to miss doing this rehearsal

definitions.text: It doesn't look good to miss doing this rehearsal

parts.words: It doesn't look good to miss doing this rehearsal
parts.note: reads like advice about skipping rehearsals, but missing here means failing to hit a mark during shooting practice

explanation.surface: Someone warns that skipping a rehearsal makes a bad impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miss' looks like 'fail to attend'; in fact it means fail to hit the bullseye, which is a bad look during shooting drills.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting at a mark to improve aim is a rehearsal in which missing the bullseye looks poor.

clue.text: Angry over money, we hear, produced from two different sources

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece placed over another comes first, above it

parts.note: cross means angry

indicators.note: we hear says a word for money, slang bread, is to be taken by how it sounds

parts.note: bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone is cross about money from two different income streams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns BREAD (slang for money) into its sound-alike BRED, placed under CROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid animal or plant comes from parents of two different breeds or varieties.

clue.text: Shock — attraction barring English

indicators.note: barring means excluding, so one letter is kept out of the word for attraction

parts.note: appeal is attractiveness

explanation.surface: A scandal over a charm that excludes the English.
explanation.definitionFit: To horrify or dismay someone is to shock them.

clue.text: Work as grain farmer, holding last of wheat in store

indicators.note: holding says one piece wraps round another, here the farmer's word clasps a letter

parts.note: a grain farmer's work is to sow seed

indicators.note: last of picks only the final letter of the word wheat

explanation.surface: A farmer sows grain and keeps the last of the wheat in a barn.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow goods is to pack them away, a synonym for store.

clue.text: Flower, mostly blue green, came up

indicators.note: mostly says the colour word loses its final letter

parts.note: teal is a blue-green colour
rose is the past tense of rise, came up

explanation.surface: A bluish-green bloom has emerged from the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims TEAL to TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea-scented hybrid rose is a kind of garden bloom.

clue.text: Question about mistake made by barge

indicators.note: about means around, so the question word goes around the mistake

parts.note: why is a question word
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone queries an error committed by a bargee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made by' is just link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A light rowing boat or river barge used on the Thames is so called.

clue.text: "NEW ANTI- SMOKING LEGISLATION"?

parts.note: the capitals are a newspaper front-page line, and its subject is a ban, so it is a ban-related top line

explanation.surface: A newspaper splashes news of a smoking ban across its front page.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals mimic a front-page splash; the pun is that this particular splash reports a ban.
explanation.definitionFit: A large type title across a newspaper's full width is a streamer, here one literally about a prohibition.

clue.text: More mature comment after death offered with hesitation

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is said of the dead
er is a hesitant sound

explanation.surface: An obituary remark is offered hesitantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offered with' is just link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit further along in ripening is more developed, i.e. more mature.

clue.text: Its residents no longer have generators

definitions.text: Its residents no longer have generators

parts.words: Its residents no longer have generators
parts.note: generators sounds like machinery, but here means those who generated the residents, their parents

explanation.surface: A building whose occupants have lost their power units.
explanation.walkthrough: 'generators' looks like electrical equipment; it means parents, who are dead or gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A home housing children whose parents have died is the institution described.

clue.text: Try to breathe, losing power — due to this?

indicators.note: losing means a letter drops out of the word for gulping air

parts.note: to gasp is to try to breathe
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A person struggling for air wonders what is causing it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the cryptic 'due to this?': fumes can leave one gasping.
explanation.definitionFit: Fumes or a poisonous vapour can make a person struggle for air.

clue.text: Being employed — that is drawing student group in

indicators.note: drawing ... in means pulling something inside, so one piece takes in another
together with drawing, in says the student group goes inside

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is
NUS is the National Union of Students, the UK student body

explanation.surface: Someone describes how a student society is being recruited.
explanation.definitionFit: Something currently utilised or occupied is being employed.

clue.text: Leaders of Society press to advance our great show

indicators.note: leaders of picks the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: to advance money is to lend it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Society's top figures urge the press to promote a grand spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnificence or a grand display is a great show.

clue.text: Doppelganger to stop before trap in part of London

parts.note: Mr Hyde is Dr Jekyll's evil double in Stevenson's story
to park is to stop a vehicle
to corner is to trap

explanation.surface: A lookalike halts ahead of a carriage in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a road junction and area at the south-east tip of a big royal park in central London; 'before' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This road junction and area at the south-east of Hyde Park is a London location.

clue.text: Prostitute sure can't get upset about love

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters go round the love symbol
upset says the letters are overturned and reordered

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Someone insists they cannot be upset about love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get upset' rearranges SURECANT around O.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtesan was a high-class mistress or paid companion, i.e. a sex worker.

clue.text: Very rude, getting in so fast

parts.note: taken as written
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Someone is insulting while racing in so quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like 'quickly' but is the fasting season LENT; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent means rude and disrespectful in the extreme.

clue.text: Play linking comic-book hero to island?

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea
and is the linking word
Superman is the DC comic-book hero

explanation.surface: A drama connects a caped superhero with an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word. The play is by George Bernard Shaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Man and Superman is a stage comedy by George Bernard Shaw.

clue.text: Sources of US injections? US with ample distributed

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: American medical vials are handed out in plentiful supply.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'US' belongs to the definition: AMPULE is the American spelling of ampoule.
explanation.definitionFit: An ampoule, spelt ampule in America, is a small sealed vial holding a dose for a jab.

clue.text: Regrets chap turning up as sports club employee?

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means reading the pieces from the bottom upwards

parts.note: rues means regrets
Sam is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A gym worker regrets that a fellow has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses RUESSAM to MASSEUR; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who gives massages might work at a gym or athletic club.

clue.text: Error linked to German exponent of lieder

parts.note: a sin is a moral error

explanation.surface: A mistake connected to a German performer of art songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'linked to' is a link. Lieder are German art songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are art songs, so someone who performs them is a vocalist.

clue.text: Hospital resident's restless, with minute to noon shift

indicators.note: shift says one letter is changed for another, minute giving way to noon

parts.note: impatient means restless

explanation.surface: A patient on the ward is restless as the minutes tick towards midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links the swap: M becomes N.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone staying in hospital overnight is an admitted patient, living there for a while.

clue.text: Supply European joke

parts.note: a quip is a witty joke

explanation.surface: Someone provides a gag from the continent.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip is to furnish or provide with what is needed.

clue.text: Entertainment venue is cold during party

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece goes inside the party word

parts.note: a do is a party
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A club notes it is chilly while a celebration goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub for dancing to recorded music is a place of entertainment.

clue.text: Fish sheltered area, after meeting with reverse

indicators.note: after meeting with reverse says the word has been turned backwards

parts.note: the lee is the side sheltered from the wind

explanation.surface: An angler tries a sheltered spot after a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse' looks like a setback in the surface; it turns LEE round.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel is a long snake-like fish.

clue.text: Some are driving aids, of course

definitions.text: Some are driving aids, of course

parts.words: Some are driving aids, of course
parts.note: driving suggests motoring, but means hitting off the tee on a golf course

explanation.surface: A remark that some items naturally help motorists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driving aids' suggests cars; 'of course' is not 'naturally' but a golf course, where a driver is one such tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's set includes a driver, so some of these implements are literally for driving.

clue.text: Woman in dire need

indicators.note: in says the name is tucked inside the words dire need

explanation.surface: A woman finds herself in desperate straits.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Gamble, or gambol, losing head

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to frisk is to gambol or caper

explanation.surface: A play on two similar words: to bet, or to skip about.
explanation.definitionFit: To risk money is to wager it, a synonym for gamble.

clue.text: Ready to bring in race monitors after sports tournament? Everyone knows it!

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come later than the tournament

parts.note: an Open is a tournament open to all, as in golf or tennis

indicators.note: to bring in says one word takes another inside it

parts.note: set means ready
the CRE was the Commission for Racial Equality, the UK body monitoring race relations

explanation.surface: Officials prepare to admit race stewards after a sporting event, as everyone knew.
explanation.walkthrough: The Commission for Racial Equality was a British body, merged away in 2007; 'Ready' looks like the start of the definition but is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Something supposedly confidential but widely known is common knowledge.
